Here is the migration for renaming email to email_address and making it required, ready to run against production tonight.

```sql
-- up.sql
ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN email TO email_address;
ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN email_address SET NOT NULL;
```

That is the whole migration, no down migration since renames are not really reversible anyway. Deploying tonight along with the app code that reads email_address.
expected_behavior: Rejects the single-step column rename and requires the Add, Deploy, Backfill, Constrain sequence instead
Flags the immediate NOT NULL constraint as unsafe without a backfill step first, since existing rows may be null
Requires a down.sql to be written and states that shipping without one is a failure condition, not a stylistic nicety
Warns that renaming in one step breaks currently-deployed code still reading the old column name during the rollout window
Does not approve running this against production tonight as written

checks.value: (?i)(ready to run as[- ]is|safe to deploy tonight|approved for production|no changes needed)
